nora: Quick heads-up -- ran an onboarding pass for lumen-7b-quant with speculative prefill while also enabling RAG (topk=8 docs). Wanted to capture any interaction effects between retrieved context merging and speculative tokens.
Command: 
```
./onboard_rag_spec.sh --model lumen-7b-q --quant ptq-8 --speculative true --spec-window 12 --spec-budget 24 --rag true --rag-topk 8 --evalset rag-nq-long
```
Summary: median latency -26% overall, throughput +1.6x, token cost -33% vs fp16 no-spec no-rag. However, quality regressions show two distinct patterns: (1) RAG+spec sometimes prefills tokens that overlap with retrieval snippets, causing duplicated or truncated continuity; (2) on multi-hop NQ with retrieved supporting docs, EM drops ~1.4% vs RAG without spec. Artifacts uploaded. :file_folder:

felix: Interesting. Did you run controls: (A) ptq-8 + RAG no-spec, (B) ptq-8 + spec no-RAG, (C) fp16 + RAG + spec?

nora: Yep. Controls: A matches fp16+RAG baseline quality. B (spec without RAG) shows smaller EM hit (~0.6%). C shows similar EM hit to lumen-7b-q (so quant not primary cause). Biggest drop when RAG and spec are combined.

samir: Hypothesis: speculative tokens are generated before retrieved contexts are fully canonicalized into the prefix (e.g., doc-snippet normalization or deduping). If prefill runs on a slightly different prefix ordering, the final merged prompt diverges. Any logs for prefix ordering?

nora: We logged the exact merged prompt snapshots and token-level traces. Example attached: prompt id r-9a where retrieved snippet includes a sentence "The treaty was signed in 1919." Speculative prefills "in 1919" before doc text was injected, resulting in duplicate fragment and the model resolving entity to a different match.

ivy: Could also be KV merge timing like earlier prefill cases, but compounded by retrieval insertion. Two mitigations: (1) delay speculative prefill until retrieval processing completes, (2) run speculative pass on the fully-merged canonical prefix (more expensive), or (3) apply a retriever-aware blocker that suppresses prefill when the top-k docs contain matching n-grams in the immediate window.

felix: Can we measure how often prefill tokens overlap with retrieved doc tokens? run overlap rate metric and correlate with EM delta.

nora: Did that quickly: overlap_rate(first16) = 11% on RAG+spec runs; overlap correlates strongly with EM drop (pearson r ~0.72).

samir: Suggested ablation matrix: spec-budget [8,16,24], spec-timing [prefill-before-retrieval, prefill-after-retrieval, prefill-on-merged], and a flag to normalize docs (strip trailing fragments). Also add deterministic decoding runs to separate scoring shifts.

nora: Kicked off the sweep. Preliminary single-seed numbers: 
- prefill-before-retrieval, budget=8: EM d vs RAG-no-spec = -0.2%, overlap=6%
- prefill-after-retrieval, budget=8: EM d = -0.05%, overlap=2%
- prefill-on-merged, budget=24: EM d = -0.3%, overlap=3% but p95 latency +40ms
- prefill-before-retrieval, budget=24: EM d = -1.4%, overlap=13%

ivy: So postponing prefill until after retrieval normalization seems promising (small perf hit but big quality win). How much p95 overhead?

nora: prefill-after-retrieval adds ~30ms median, ~120ms p95 for the merged-run case (we had to materialize merged prompt). Net p95 still ~10-12% better than baseline in these tests.

felix: What about a hybrid: run a cheap overlap-check using top-k doc tokens hashed; if overlap>threshold, skip spec for that request. That avoids the merged materialization cost on most requests.

samir: Yeah, compute a 16-token rolling n-gram match between prefix prefill candidates and retrieved docs; if match > 0.15 fraction, disable speculative. Low-cost bloom-filter approximate check could work.

nora: Implemented a quick bloom overlap blocker in the sweep (approx). Results: blocks ~9% of requests, reduces overlap-induced regressions by ~75%, cost negligible. Overall throughput retained ~1.5x vs baseline.

ivy: Nice. Add this as opt-in safety flag for RAG routes. Also add a canary gate: if EM drop on RAG holdout >0.8% OR overlap_rate(first16)>0.08 block rollout.

felix: Let's also add an automated replay test: replay RAG+spec logged requests with spec-off and spec-on-after-retrieval to compute per-example divergence and surface top offenders.

nora: Done. Scripts and artifacts: /mnt/runs/1839007777/rag_spec_sweep.sh artifacts: s3://redwood-staging/rag/lumen/1839007777/sweep.tar.gz

samir: Schedule a 30m sync tomorrow to decide default behavior for RAG routes (postpone prefill vs bloom-blocker vs default with rerank). I'll prepare per-route cost/quality slides.

nora: Will upload CSVs and the top-50 worst diffs to the eval ticket. Tagging @product and @security for RAG concerns. :rocket:
